question: Which part of the human eye does the most work when focusing light?
explanation: Spot on! The cornea is that clear, curved window at the front of the eye that does the heavy lifting of bending light rays before they even reach the lens.

question: What is the main job of the rod cells in your retina?

options.A: Processing sharp color details in bright light
options.C: Controlling the size of the pupil

explanation: You got it! Rods are your night-vision heroes. They are super sensitive to dim light, helping you see in the dark and catch movement out of the corner of your eye.

question: Which part of the eye makes the watery fluid (aqueous humor)?
explanation: Great job! The ciliary body acts like a little factory, constantly making aqueous humor to nourish the inside parts of the eye.

question: What happens inside the eye if the fluid drainage gets blocked while the eye keeps making more fluid?
explanation: Spot on! If fluid keeps pouring in but cannot flow out, it backs up and causes the pressure inside the eye to rise.

question: Which type of glaucoma happens suddenly and comes with severe pain because the drainage angle is completely blocked?
explanation: That's right! In angle-closure glaucoma, the iris suddenly blocks the drainage path, trapping fluid and causing a painful, emergency spike in eye pressure.

question: A patient has chronic open-angle glaucoma. Which part of their vision usually fades first?
explanation: Correct! Open-angle glaucoma is sneaky; it slowly steals side vision first, long before the person notices any trouble with their central view.

question: What actually causes a cataract to form in the eye?

options.A: Optic nerve fibers swell and snap
options.B: The cornea loses its outer layer
options.C: The eye stops making fluid completely
options.D: Proteins in the lens clump together and get cloudy

explanation: You nailed it! Over time, proteins inside the natural lens can clump up, turning clear glass into a cloudy windshield.

question: Why do people with early cataracts often complain about blinding glare when driving at night?

options.A: The pupil refuses to open in the dark
options.B: Extra eye fluid spills over the cornea
options.C: Cloudy proteins in the lens scatter incoming light
options.D: The retina loses all of its cone cells

explanation: Spot on! Instead of letting headlights pass cleanly through, those cloudy clumps scatter the light everywhere, creating a blinding glare for the driver.

question: What are the small, yellowish deposits that build up under the retina in dry age-related macular degeneration called?
explanation: Great work! Drusen are tiny fatty deposits that collect under the retina as we age. Finding them is a key sign of dry macular degeneration.

question: A patient says they feel like a dark curtain or shadow is moving across their vision. What emergency should you suspect?
explanation: Spot on! That classic 'curtain falling' description is a textbook warning sign that the retina is peeling away from the back of the eye. It's a medical emergency!

question: What do we call inflammation of the middle layer of the eye, which includes the iris?
explanation: You got it! Uveitis is inflammation of the uvea (the middle layer). It can cause a deep, aching pain and make the eyes very sensitive to light.

question: Why do deep scratches or infections on the cornea take so long to heal?

options.B: Tears wash away all the healing white blood cells
options.C: The cornea does not have its own blood supply
options.D: Eye germs are immune to normal inflammation

explanation: Correct! Because the cornea has no blood vessels of its own, infection-fighting cells and nutrients have to travel a long way from nearby tissues, slowing down healing.

question: Why is looking into a patient's eye with an ophthalmoscope so useful for checking whole-body health?

options.A: The eye mirrors the brain with 100% perfection
options.B: It lets doctors look directly at living tiny blood vessels and nerves
options.C: It is the only organ affected by high blood sugar
options.D: It has the most pain receptors in the body

explanation: Spot on! Because the eye is clear, healthcare workers can peer right inside to see how tiny blood vessels are doing without cutting anything open.

question: Which eye finding is most often seen in a patient with poorly controlled high blood pressure?

options.C: Cloudy protein clumps in the lens

explanation: You nailed it! High pressure can strain tiny retinal blood vessels until they burst, creating little flame-shaped bleeds that show up during an eye exam.

question: Why should a nurse gently press the inner corner of the eye (punctal occlusion) right after giving eye drops?

options.A: To make the eye produce more fluid
options.C: To keep the medicine from getting into the rest of the body
options.D: To keep the pupil wide open

explanation: Great job! Pressing the tear duct blocks the drop from draining down into the nose and entering the bloodstream, preventing unwanted side effects.

question: A patient who just had cataract surgery asks why they must avoid heavy lifting. What is the best nursing response?

options.B: Bending over can cause pink eye
options.C: Lifting dries out the surface of your eye
options.D: Straining raises your eye pressure and can pop the healing stitches

explanation: Spot on! Straining, heavy lifting, or bending down spikes the pressure inside the eye, which can easily damage fresh surgical cuts.
